newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine peso ends steady, central bank buys dlr.
newsitem.headline: Philippine peso ends steady, central bank buys dlr.

text.p: The Philippine peso ended at its previous day's level of 26.235 pesos as the Central Bank kept buying dollars at that rate, traders said on Thursday.
The day's average was also at 26.235 to the dollar from 26.232 on Wednesday, with turnover thinning to $128.90 million from $190.20 million.
A local bank dealer said banks continued to sell their dollars in exchange for pesos to ease their liquidity situation.
Banks grappled with tight peso liquidity in recent days after investing in dollars and T-bills.
Another trader said the market view is now for the peso to appreciate. "The thing is there is not much pressure for the dollar to go up. There are not many buyers (of dollars)."
Foreign funds, with interest rate arbitrage positions, have already departed, and dollar inflows have become steady again, the same dealer said.
Traders estimate the Central bank bought $41.5 million at 26.245 pesos.
